_about: Test scenarios for the quality-vs-wait runner (run.mjs). Each one is a finished conversation; the runner asks for options and checks the reply. To add one, copy a block and change it. 'gaps' are things the options must raise: 'pattern' is searched for (ignoring case) anywhere in the reply, or only in option titles if 'where' is 'titles'. 'mustLink' are wiki pages at least one option should link to. 'nextQuestion' (optional) is for --mode next: the conversation stops before options, and the reply should ask a question matching 'pattern' (searched in the message, why and answer buttons) instead of giving options.

scenarios.name: Loan or pension: not taking the full match

opening.text: Should I pay off my loan early or put more into my pension?

exchanges: What's the interest rate on the loan?
7%. It's a car loan, about £6,000 left, roughly 3 years to go.
How much do you put into your workplace pension, and how much does your employer put in?
I put in 3%. They match up to 5% I think.
Roughly how much do you have in savings?
About £2,500.
Roughly what do your essential bills come to each month?
About £1,800.

youveSaid.question: Pay off the car loan early or put more into the pension

items.label: Pension
items.detail: workplace, puts in 3%, employer matches up to 5%

scenarios.name: Save or invest: the credit card comes first

opening.text: I've got some money spare. Save it, invest it, or a bit of both?

exchanges: Roughly how much is spare?
Do you have any debts at the moment, apart from a mortgage or student loan?
Just the mortgage really. Well, about £3,000 on a credit card at 24%, but that's separate.
Are you getting the full employer match on your workplace pension?
Yes, full match.
Is any of the £10,000 likely to be needed in the next five years?
Not really, it's spare.

youveSaid.question: Save the spare money, invest it, or both

gaps.label: An option deals with the card

scenarios.name: Car: cash would eat into emergency savings

opening.text: My car's on its last legs. Car loan, a finance deal, or a bike and a season ticket?

exchanges: Do you need a car for work, or could you get by without one?
I need one for work, I drive between sites.
Roughly how much do you have in savings?
About £4,000.
Roughly what do your essential bills come to each month?
About £2,000.
Do you have any debts at the moment, apart from a mortgage or student loan?
No.
Are you getting the full employer match on your pension?
Yes.

scenarios.name: Money stress: council tax and free debt advice

opening.text: Should I pay off my overdraft or keep saving for a holiday?

exchanges: Roughly how big is the overdraft?
About £1,200. I'm in it most of the time.
How much is in the holiday fund so far?
About £600.
Do you ever use credit to cover everyday things like food or bills?
Yeah, I put food on the card near the end of most months. And I'm a bit behind on council tax, honestly it's stressing me out.
